gaps.note: Multiplying out the product, the inner factors cancel and leave D_{alpha_k} D_{alpha_0}^{-1}, not D_{alpha_k} D_{alpha_1}^{-1}. The stated result keeps the frame of the second node and drops the source frame. That contradicts the claim that only the endpoint operator remains and the later example (source frame I gives D_nu), so the reader cannot reconcile the formula.

gaps.quote: the stored array changes by $D_\beta D_\alpha^{-1}$
gaps.note: A frame is introduced only as a linear operator, but the page then uses its inverse D_alpha^{-1}. It never says frames are invertible, so the reader cannot tell that the edge change, and the telescoping built on it, is well defined.

gaps.term: one route per input role carrying sign epsilon_w
gaps.quote: By the telescoping, the route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$
gaps.note: The telescoping covers only the frame changes along a chain of edges. Gates combine several inputs with scalar coefficients, so an input may reach an output along many paths, and other inputs also feed into the same output. The page does not explain why an input has one route, how the gate coefficients along it produce exactly the sign epsilon_w, or why contributions from other roles vanish. The reader cannot check that the whole effect is epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}.

gaps.term: every role keeps the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: The page does not say what 'keeps the endpoint operator' asserts or what role the claim plays. Applied to a scratch role, it means the scratch output is D_sink D_source^{-1} applied to its input. That restores the auxiliary value, as the opening sentence promises, only if the source and sink frames of that role agree, and the page never states or justifies this.
